Hook p99 396 ms of a 2500 ms budget

label: The live brief over all 44 typed rows is 306 bytes at the median, 337 at p95 and 350 at the maximum, with a head median of 88 bytes, p95 119 and max 132; all 44 rendered a live head, closing the phase 015 degraded_brief limitation with a number.
About 72 percent of every brief is the fixed comment-hygiene directive: the no-match brief is 244 bytes (25 head plus 219 directive), and at the 306-byte median the recommendation is about 87 bytes.

Hook latency has wide headroom: 1826 real health records from 2026-11-13 give median 178 ms, p95 294 ms, p99 396 ms and max 893 ms, with zero records over 1000 ms and zero over the 2500 ms budget; the in-process handler over 44 live calls is 145.3 ms median, 233.5 p95 and 274 max.
The brief is selective: 325 of 1826 records emitted a non-zero brief (17.8 percent), mean 265.6 bytes per emission and 47.3 bytes per record, with 47 stale, 19 fail-open and 6 degraded records.

No byte cut is worth building: the only removable head decoration left is about 30 bytes of 306 (9.8 percent) and removing it loses freshness and the pass mark, while the other 219 bytes are the directive block whose trimming was decided in segment one.
